headline: NASA RFPs. Northrop Grumman wins. True Anomaly raises.
deck: This week saw significant contracts and funding shifts in the space sector.

stories.head: Northrop Grumman bags $398 million satellite deal
stories.body: The U.S. Space Force awarded Northrop Grumman a $398 million contract for satellite testing, underscoring the company's ongoing role in the military space landscape. This win comes as the Space Force continues to prioritize satellite capabilities amidst shifting defense needs. As competition heats up, Grumman's established relationships may prove more valuable than cutting-edge tech.
stories.soWhat: In a sector where new entrants often steal the spotlight, established players like Northrop Grumman are still cashing in on their legacy.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190 million Series C
stories.body: True Anomaly secured $190 million in a Series C funding round, bringing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The company focuses on co-orbital security and space domain awareness, appealing to defense budgets eager to bolster capabilities. Investors seem to be betting that co-orbital threats will remain a top priority for the DoD.
stories.soWhat: True Anomaly's funding shows that even in a crowded market, niche players can thrive by aligning closely with defense needs.

stories.head: NASA issues RFP for Mars communications orbiter
stories.body: NASA released its final RFP for a Mars communications orbiter, inviting bids from companies eager to enhance interplanetary communication. This move indicates a continued commitment to Mars exploration, with potential contracts likely exceeding previous missions' budgets. The stakes are high as firms scramble to showcase their best ideas.
stories.soWhat: With the competition for Mars contracts heating up, expect to see some wild proposals that may or may not involve sending Wi-Fi to the Red Planet.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on SpaceX's valuation
watchlist.body: With its secondary market valuation hitting $470 billion, SpaceX is a bellwether for investor sentiment in aerospace.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: Their joint bid for the SDA constellation could signal a shift in how defense contractors approach satellite projects.

watchlist.title: FY27 budget implications
watchlist.body: The additional $1.4 billion for space resilience could reshape procurement strategies across the defense sector.

watchlist.title: Watch for GPS jamming trends
watchlist.body: The return of GPS jamming in the Eastern Med could prompt new strategies in navigation and satellite operations.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
